translationRepairs: Emperor Wu received him in audience. Andou asked permission to return north and raise rebellion along the Yellow River and in Shaanxi, rallying loyal partisans.
Emperor Wen received him in audience. Andou asked permission to return north and raise rebellion along the Yellow River and in Shaanxi, rallying loyal partisans.
In the Songshu, Taizu is Liu Yilong, Emperor Wen; the surrounding Yuanjia chronology confirms that he, not Emperor Wu, received Xue Andou.
The Founding Emperor received him in audience; [Andou] asked to return north to stir up trouble in the He and Shaanxi regions and gather loyal followers.
The Grand Ancestor (Taizu) received him in audience; [Andou] asked to return north to stir up trouble in the He and Shaanxi regions and gather loyal followers.
太祖 is the temple name Taizu and refers here to Emperor Wen. 'Founding Emperor' incorrectly points to Emperor Wu, whose temple name is Gaozu.
Shuang sent his general Zheng Dexuan to garrison Great Xian. Dexuan dispatched his vanguard Yang Hu with light troops toward Liyang.
Shuang sent his general Zheng Dexuan to garrison Great Xian. Dexuan dispatched his vanguard Yang Huyu with light troops toward Liyang.
The following sentence shortens 楊胡與 to 胡與, confirming that the full personal name is Yang Huyu rather than Yang Hu.
Andou sent Zong Yue and Liyang Administrator Cheng Tianzuo to intercept and rout them, beheading Yang Hu and his second-in-command.
Andou sent Zong Yue and Liyang Administrator Cheng Tianzuo to intercept and rout them, beheading Hu Yu and his second-in-command.
胡與 is the shortened form of Yang Huyu's name, not Yang Hu.

Earlier, Andou's nephew by marriage Suo'er had served during the Jinghe era of Emperor Qianfei as vanguard general and direct attendant, joined in the slaughter of the princes and high ministers, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wu'an county with a fief of three hundred households.

Earlier, Andou's agnatic nephew Suo'er had served during the Jinghe era of Emperor Qianfei as vanguard general and direct attendant, joined in the slaughter of the princes and high ministers, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wu'an county with a fief of three hundred households.
從子 denotes a nephew in the paternal line, not a nephew by marriage. 'Agnatic nephew' preserves the relationship without over-specifying which brother was his father.
Shen Wenxiu, whose courtesy name was Zhongyuan, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery and was a disciple of Minister of Works Shen Qingzhi.
Shen Wenxiu, whose courtesy name was Zhongyuan, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery and was a son of Minister of Works Shen Qingzhi's younger brother.
Here 弟子 is a kinship expression: Wenxiu was the son of Qingzhi's younger brother, not Qingzhi's disciple. The proposal's doubled title does not fix the real error.

In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi Xunyang was pacified. Emperor Ming sent Ministerial Clerk for Revenue Cui Yuansun to reward the loyalist armies. He was killed in defeat alongside Senghao and was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.

In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, Xunyang was pacified. Emperor Ming sent Cui Yuansun, a ministerial clerk in the Revenue Bureau, to commend the loyalist armies. He accompanied Senghao, was defeated in battle, and was killed; he was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.
A comma must separate the Taishi date from Xunyang. The revision also renders 隨僧皓戰敗見殺 in sequence and 追贈 as a posthumous appointment rather than an enfeoffment.
